title_seen: Quantization and Training of Neural Networks for Efficient Integer-Arithmetic-Only Inference
work_done: Defines the affine scheme r = S(q - Z) with integer-only inference: uint8 operands, int32 accumulation, int32 bias with S_bias = S1*S2, and requantization by a fixed-point multiplier M0 in [0.5,1) plus a rounding shift, followed by a saturating cast; adds quantization-aware training.
advantages: Whole layer (MAC, bias, requant, ReLU6 clamp) runs in integer arithmetic, so a bit-exact integer reference is possible; small loss (ResNet-50 ImageNet 74.9% vs 76.4% float).
disadvantages: Evaluated on ARM CPUs (Snapdragon 835 cores) rather than accelerator hardware; scheme uses uint8 with zero-points, which adds zero-point correction terms.
relevance: Method we reuse: standard integer-only requantization (int32 accumulator, fixed-point multiplier and shift) behind V3's bit-exact INT8 path.
read_locator: full text: Sec. 2.1-2.4, Sec. 3, Table 4.1, Fig. 4.1 (arXiv v1)

title_seen: DSP-Packing: Squeezing Low-precision Arithmetic into FPGA DSP Blocks
work_done: Generalizes Xilinx's INT8/INT4 multiplication packing on the DSP48E2 to arbitrary bit widths and counts, analyses its rounding error, proposes full and approximate corrections, and introduces approximate 'Overpacking' (six 4-bit multiplies per DSP).
advantages: Shows the vendor INT4 packing has an error bounded by -1 (MAE 0.37) and gives a full correction costing 27 LUTs and 32 FFs that reaches zero error; packing density analysed per method.
disadvantages: Circuit-level study on one Zynq UltraScale+ device (XCZU7EV), no full CNN accelerator; Overpacking is approximate and therefore not bit-exact.
relevance: Method source: exactness conditions and correction for packed INT8 MACs in V3's DSP48E2 PEs; Overpacking is a contrast (inexact).
read_locator: full text: Sec. II-VII, Table I, Fig. 9 (arXiv v1)

title_seen: RiSA: A Reinforced Systolic Array for Depthwise Convolutions and Embedded Tensor Reshaping
work_done: Presents RiSA, a systolic-array DNN accelerator with a mechanism that raises PE utilization for depthwise convolutions and performs tensor reshaping inside the PE array instead of in a separate module.
advantages: Minimal-overhead depthwise support on a systolic array; supports CNNs and NLP models; 1.91x area and 1.31x energy efficiency over Eyeriss v2 on MobileNet-V1.
disadvantages: Comparison is against Eyeriss v2 for MobileNet-V1; abstract gives no FPGA implementation or latency-bound details.
relevance: Closest prior work for V3's depthwise mode on an output-stationary systolic array.
notes: ACM TECS. Full text not fetched.

title_seen: ShortcutFusion: From Tensorflow to FPGA-Based Accelerator With a Reuse-Aware Memory Allocation for Shortcut Data
work_done: Compiler plus FPGA accelerator that statically allocates on-chip buffers for residual shortcut data and fuses the element-wise addition with the convolution, choosing row- or frame-based weight reuse per block; INT8 on a KCU1500 at 200 MHz.
advantages: Fused CONV+shortcut needs one write and two reads instead of two writes and three reads off-chip, no extra element-wise latency; DRAM access reduced 47.8-84.8% for RetinaNet, YOLOv3, ResNet152, EfficientNet.
disadvantages: Targets large networks and a data-center card (KCU1500), not an embedded Zynq; evaluation focuses on throughput and DRAM traffic, not latency predictability.
relevance: Residual-add hardware: fused element-wise add and on-chip shortcut buffering, compared with V3's residual handling for ResNet-20.
read_locator: full text: Sec. III-IV (element-wise chain, shortcut reuse), result tables (arXiv v4 of the TCSI paper)
notes: Read arXiv v4; published version is IEEE TCAS-I 2022. Also uses the 2-INT8-per-DSP48E2 packing.

title_seen: A White Paper on Neural Network Quantization
work_done: Tutorial white paper: hardware-motivated introduction (accelerator with 32-bit accumulators and requantization), uniform affine, symmetric and power-of-two quantizers, per-tensor vs per-channel, then PTQ (range setting, cross-layer equalization, bias correction, AdaRound) and QAT pipelines.
advantages: Explains the hardware cost of asymmetric weights and per-channel scales; states that PTQ is in most cases sufficient for 8-bit with close to floating-point accuracy; gives tested pipelines.
disadvantages: arXiv white paper, not peer reviewed; algorithmic focus, evaluated with simulated quantization rather than on a specific accelerator.
relevance: Background for V3's INT8 format choice (symmetric weights, per-tensor vs per-channel, 32-bit accumulators).
notes: No DOI; arXiv only. Krishnamoorthi 2018 (1806.08342) is an alternative, see notes.

title_seen: Double MAC on a DSP: Boosting the Performance of Convolutional Neural Networks on FPGAs
work_done: Proposes double MAC, packing two multiply-and-accumulate operations into one FPGA DSP block, exploiting the CNN accelerator's mode of operation; validated by synthesis and Verilog simulation in a state-of-the-art CNN accelerator.
advantages: Can double the computation throughput of a CNN layer; network-level gain of 14% to more than 80% depending on network and FPGA size.
disadvantages: Relies on tolerance to small numerical errors ('without sacrificing the output quality significantly'), so not presented as bit-exact; validated by synthesis and simulation, not board measurement.
relevance: DSP-packing prior work; contrast with V3's exact packing requirement.
read_locator: abstract (Semantic Scholar API record of the TCAD paper)

title_seen: Revealing Untapped DSP Optimization Potentials for FPGA-Based Systolic Matrix Engines
work_done: Analyses DSP48E2 features for systolic engines: in-DSP operand prefetching for weight-stationary arrays (TPUv1-like) and, for the output-stationary Vitis AI DPUCZDX8G engine (INT8 packing plus DSP double-pumping), in-DSP multiplexing and a ring accumulator.
advantages: Against a replica of the DPU B1024 array: 85% fewer LUTs, 20% fewer FFs, half the DSP accumulators and 20% less power at the same clock.
disadvantages: Reduces bias and accumulator precision to INT24 (stated minor precision loss); results are out-of-context Vivado implementations of the array only, not full accelerators on a board.
relevance: Explains the DPU baseline's INT8 packing and double-pumping; DSP techniques applicable to V3's OS array.
read_locator: full text: Sec. III-VII, Table II (arXiv v1)

title_seen: A High-Performance CNN Processor Based on FPGA for MobileNets
work_done: FPGA CNN processor for MobileNets with two dedicated engines, a Conv Engine for pointwise and a Dwcv Engine for depthwise convolution, a schedule between them, and Channel Augmentation for the first layer; implemented on ZU2 and ZU9 MPSoCs.
advantages: ImageNet classification at 205.3 fps (ZU2) and 809.8 fps (ZU9), 15.4x and 60.7x over CPU; MobileNet+SSD at 31.0 and 124.3 fps.
disadvantages: Separate depthwise engine costs dedicated hardware; evaluation is MobileNet/ImageNet throughput against CPU only (from the abstract).
relevance: Contrast: separate depthwise engine versus V3's depthwise mode in the shared array; DPU-lineage design on Zynq UltraScale+.

title_seen: Shortcut Mining: Exploiting Cross-Layer Shortcut Reuse in DCNN Accelerators
work_done: Proposes Shortcut Mining: logical buffers and a sequence of procedures that keep shortcut (residual) and non-shortcut feature maps on chip across any number of intermediate layers without extra buffer resources; prototyped on FPGAs.
advantages: Off-chip feature-map traffic reduced 53.3%, 58% and 43% for SqueezeNet, ResNet-34 and ResNet-152, with 1.93x throughput over a state-of-the-art accelerator.
disadvantages: Focus on off-chip traffic for large ImageNet networks; abstract gives no precision or latency-predictability details.
relevance: Residual-shortcut handling prior work (on-chip shortcut reuse) relevant to V3's ResNet-20 residual path.
read_locator: abstract (Semantic Scholar API record of the HPCA paper)
notes: Spare. ShortcutFusion builds on and compares with it.
